prompt: Implement the nexus vitals health gate per ADR-2026-06-04-1740. Five tasks, in priority order. (1) FIX THE BUSY-SPIN [DONE 2026-06-04 — jemalloc shipped, idle CPU 600%->0%, validated; remaining sub-item (b) typed-deserialize is lower priority]: nexus burned ~6 cores at idle via glibc malloc ARENA-LOCK CONTENTION. perf(symbol build)+perf trace proved it: self-CPU = serde_json::Value::clone/deserialize_any/drop + _int_malloc/_int_free + __lll_lock_wait_private; one worker did 331848 futex/4s (36% EAGAIN). Driver = every STDB adapter parses SQL into untyped serde_json::Value (sql_query()->Vec<Value>) + clones rows, called by ~20 short-interval polls (org_responder 4s, supervisor/integrator 5s, etc.) on SELECT * of growing tables (rl_q_entry, rl_pattern, agent, message, workplan_task); all funneled through 2 arenas because nexus.rs:417 sets MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2 (ADR-2026-05-22-1720). PROVEN: restart with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=16 => idle CPU 600%->0% (RSS 1.1GB). The arena cap is the wrong lever (trades CPU vs the 25GB RSS bloat it was added to fix). FIX (supersede ADR-2026-05-22-1720): (a) swap global allocator to jemalloc/mimalloc (per-thread caches, no global arena-lock storm) — fixes BOTH the RSS fragmentation AND the contention, then REMOVE MALLOC_ARENA_MAX; validate over a multi-hour run that RSS stays bounded AND idle CPU low. (b) reduce allocation rate: deserialize STDB rows into typed structs via serde derive (not Value+clone); widen/cache the 4-5s polls or move to STDB push-subscriptions instead of SELECT * polling. Add a regression test asserting idle nexus CPU < ceiling. INTERIM: live daemon currently running MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=16 (relieved, non-durable — nexus.rs:417 reverts to 2 on normal restart). (2) AUTO-CALIBRATE PROVIDERS [DONE operationally 2026-06-04 — only the automation remains]: root cause is config_sync.rs:248 preloads providers and preserves existing scores but registers new/uncalibrated ones at default 0.0 and NEVER triggers calibration; calibrate-all only fires on manual POST /api/inference/calibrate-all or `hex inference test`, so providers sit at q=0.00 forever. Running calibrate-all by hand fixed 3/4 instantly (qwen2.5-coder 0.85, Qwen3-32B 0.92, DeepSeek-R1 0.99; qwen3.6:35b-a3b was true-OOM and de-registered). FIX: after config_sync preload and on any provider registration, best-effort async-trigger calibrate-all for providers at the uncalibrated-default score; introduce a sentinel (e.g. -1.0) to distinguish 'never calibrated' from a real scored 0.0 so routing/health-gate can tell them apart. NOTE: the 'model=probe -> HTTP 404' startup log line is an UNRELATED health-check, not the calibration path — do not chase it. (3) AUTO-RELEASE GUARD: hex-cli/src/commands/nexus.rs find_nexus_binary() resolves [debug, release] — make the --daemon path prefer target/release (debug only via explicit HEX_NEXUS_BIN or a --dev flag) and warn loudly if a debug binary is ever resolved as a daemon. (4) HARD HEALTH GATE: add `hex doctor vitals` (also run at swarm-dispatch, surfaced by hex go / hex pulse) that HARD-FAILS on: nexus self-CPU over threshold while no inference is in flight, any provider q=0.00, STDB unreachable, or debug-build daemon. (5) PRODUCTIVITY WATCHDOG: nexus background task flags any swarm 'active' > N hours with zero commits AND zero completed tasks, auto-pauses it, and raises a priority-2 inbox notification. (6) PURGE COMPLETED/STALE AGENT ROWS [gap found 2026-06-04; reaped by hand once, WILL recur]: the agent-registry.agent table accumulated 7548 rows (only 6 real processes) since 2026-05-27 — 6647 status='completed' session rows that never got ended_at stamped + ~896 phantom 'registered' (processId 0, no heartbeat) + 116 'dead'. Root cause: run_agent_cleanup (spacetime-modules/agent-registry/src/lib.rs:154) ONLY transitions registered/active/stale agents that HAVE a heartbeat (registered->stale->dead); it never DELETES rows and never touches status='completed' (which isn't even in VALID_AGENT_STATUSES). The only delete reducer is remove_agent(id), one at a time. This bloat directly fed the busy-spin: GET /api/agents = SELECT * FROM agent parsed into serde_json::Value on every poll. Manual reap 2026-06-04: looped remove_agent over all-but-the-6-live ids (9ms/call, ~70s) -> table back to 6; also `hex swarm cleanup --apply` reconciled 3 abandoned swarms. FIX (build the verb per CLAUDE.md): add a bulk `purge_agents_by_status(statuses, older_than)` reducer to agent-registry that deletes completed/dead rows (and registered rows with empty last_seen older than a cutoff) in one transaction, plus their agent_heartbeat rows; call it periodically from the orphan_reaper/zombie_sweeper loop (NOT every tick — e.g. every 5 min) and expose `hex agent purge [--status] [--older-than]`. Also fix the upstream leak: stamp ended_at when an agent session completes so rows don't sit as completed-but-unended forever. Requires rebuilding+republishing the agent-registry WASM module (hex stdb publish). The hard-health-gate (task 4) should also flag agent-row count over a ceiling as a vitals warning. (7) SURFACE OPERATOR ESCALATIONS + CATCH TOOL-ROUND-TRIP CHURN [found via live test 2026-06-04]: dispatched a small bounded task (write one unit test for compute_quality_score) to hex-coder via `hex ops send`; the SOP loop picked it up but the agent burned the 16 tool-round-trip cap on local Ollama (sop_executor: 'Ollama-first failed; escalating to paid tier error=tool round-trip cap (16)'), escalated to Qwen3-32B, kept looping, and raised 8 escalate_to_operator events — EVERY one tagged 'logged; dashboard wiring deferred'. Net: the requested file was never written, but the loop auto-committed an UNRELATED ADR doc edit (action#8448). Two fixes: (a) WIRE escalate_to_operator TO THE DASHBOARD/INBOX — when an agent is stuck and asks the operator, it must appear in the dashboard (and `hex inbox`), not die in a log line (the tool already exists in hex-nexus/src/tools/escalate_to_operator.rs; finish the surface). (b) PRODUCTIVITY/CHURN SIGNAL: when a persona hits the tool-round-trip cap and escalates >N times without producing a code_patch/commit on the dispatched intent, raise a priority-2 inbox notification and pause that intent (fold into task 5's watchdog) — the doer looping on the SOP tool protocol is the execution-layer failure that remains after the substrate fixes. HARD CONSTRAINT: cargo build -p hex-nexus --release and cargo build -p hex-cli --release must exit 0; agent-registry WASM must publish clean; add tests for tasks 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.
notes: Authored from the 2026-06-04 operator autopsy: 5-day debug daemon, zero swarm output, 3/4 providers q=0.00, silent ~6-core busy-spin, 7548 phantom agent rows. PROGRESS as of 2026-06-04: task 1 (busy-spin) DONE via jemalloc (committed, branch fix/nexus-jemalloc-arena-spin, idle CPU 0%); task 2 inference calibration done operationally (3 providers 0.85-0.99), only the auto-trigger automation remains; agent reap + swarm reconcile done by hand (registry 7548->6). REMAINING to build: task 3 (auto-release guard), task 4 (hex doctor vitals hard gate), task 5 (productivity watchdog), task 6 (purge_agents_by_status reducer + periodic call + ended_at stamping), task 7 (surface escalate_to_operator to dashboard/inbox + tool-round-trip churn signal — found via live test), and the automation halves of tasks 1b/2. Highest-leverage next item = task 7a (make stuck-agent escalations visible). All remaining tasks executable; inference healthy.
